A catalytic converter in the automobile exhaust system oxidizes carbon monoxide (CO) to carbon dioxide (CO₂).
Solar energy can be used to generate electricity, heat water, and cook food.
The air quality index (AQI) is a scale that indicates the level of air pollution. It conveys how clean or polluted the air is and the associated health risk.

High-risk groups include children, older adults, people with heart or lung diseases, and people exposed to pollution for long periods, such as outdoor workers. Pollution can harm their health more severely because their bodies may be more vulnerable or their exposure may be greater.

Strategies include planting trees, using catalytic converters to reduce harmful vehicle emissions, and reducing sulphur dioxide emissions from flue gases. Using renewable resources is another strategy.

Major causes include vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, emissions from coal-fired power plants, and smoke and particulate matter from sources such as burning fuels. Winter conditions can trap pollutants near the ground, allowing them to build up.
